input.quote: However, any Party may terminate its participation in this Agreement at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter by giving not less than one (1) year's prior notice thereof, in writing, to the other Parties.
input.rationale: Paragraph 18 locks us into a twenty-five (25) year Initial Period with no unilateral exit: termination of participation is available only at the end of the Initial Period or thereafter on one year's notice (18.1), and mid-term termination requires unanimous written agreement of all Parties (18.2). That is the playbook walk-away case — no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term. Given the consortium construction-and-maintenance bargain, a 30-day preferred exit would be disproportionate, so we redline to the fallback: a Customer convenience exit on 90 days' notice with any early-termination fee capped at three (3) months' fees, and Vendor convenience termination confined to the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice.

mappings.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees.
Vendor termination for convenience only at the end of a term.
90 days' notice for Vendor termination for convenience.

ops.text: Customer may terminate its participation in this Agreement for convenience at any time, including during the Initial Period, by giving not less than 90 days' prior notice, in writing, to the other Parties, and any early-termination fee payable by Customer by reason of such termination shall not exceed three (3) months' fees. Vendor may terminate for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term, on not less than 90 days' prior written notice.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The 25-year Initial Period leaves us no exit except unanimous agreement, so we have added a Customer convenience termination right on 90 days' notice with any early-termination fee capped at three (3) months' fees, and limited Vendor's convenience termination to the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice. This is our fallback position.
proposal.summary: Insert a Customer convenience exit on 90 days' notice with any early-termination fee capped at three months' fees, and confine Vendor convenience termination to the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice.
